newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador announces tame fiscal measures.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador announces tame fiscal measures.

text.p: Ecuador's President Fabian Alarcon announced a tame package of economic measures Thursday evening to help plug the country's fiscal deficit.

Profit margins in the petrol business will be trimmed, raising state revenues by 0.3 percent of gross domestic product, while electricity subsidies would be reduced contributing 0.4 percent of GDP, Alarcon said.
"The government is eliminating the subsidy for those sectors which can pay, and maintaining it for the working class," he said.
The whole package of measures is expected to boost government revenues by 1.9 percent of GDP.
"The government has made an original effort to prevent the measures from hitting the poorest sectors of the population in 24 hours," Alarcon told reporters.
The government expects to collect another 0.5 percent of GDP by introducing new petrol merchandising rules and said it would stop using income from crude exports to buy derivatives.
"Suppliers themselves should be the ones who finance imports of gas and diesel, freeing up 0.3 percent of GDP," Alarcon said.
He also ratified an earlier announcement to collect a $57 million debt from electricity firm Emelec, a payment which he said would generate revenues of 0.3 percent of GDP.
Alarcon said the government would continue to enforce its austerity policy and expected Customs tax collection to improve, but he did not rule out future rises in domestic gas prices.
The government inherited a budget deficit of 6.6-6.9 percent of GDP when it took over from former President Abala Bucram in February.
The deficit is now at 4.6 percent of GDP, after a 10 percent reduction in public spending and improved tax collection, but Alarcon hopes to squeeze the gap to 2.7 percent by the end of the year.
This year's GDP is estimated at $19.9 billion.
